meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'money', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Мы столько денег зря сегодня угробили!
examples.trans: We wasted so much money for nothing today!

examples.text: Продам камни, а деньги поделим поровну.
examples.trans: I will sell the stones, and we will split the money equally.

examples.text: У меня нет денег.
examples.trans: I have no money.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'for nothing'.

examples.text: Мы столько денег зря сегодня угробили!
examples.trans: We wasted so much money for nothing today!

examples.text: У тебя есть время, не теряй его зря.
examples.trans: You still have time, do not waste it in vain.

examples.text: Вы зря теряете время.
examples.trans: You're wasting your time.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Помнишь, ты мне сегодня рыбу привозил?
examples.trans: Do you remember you brought me fish today?

examples.text: Мы столько денег зря сегодня угробили!
examples.trans: We wasted so much money for nothing today!

examples.text: Ну, видимо, потому что сегодня четверг.
examples.trans: Well, apparently because today is Thursday.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (root 'гробить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'ruin'.

examples.text: Мы столько денег зря сегодня угробили!
examples.trans: We wasted so much money for nothing today!

examples.text: Ты человека чуть не угробил.
examples.trans: You nearly killed a man.

examples.text: Ты своей глупой шуткой человека чуть не угробил!
examples.trans: With your foolish prank you nearly got a man killed!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'a little'.

examples.text: Подожди, чуть позже всё сделаем.
examples.trans: Wait, we will do everything a little later.

examples.text: Чуть позже схожу в ломбард.
examples.trans: A little later I will go to the pawnshop.

examples.text: Я чуть не упал.
examples.trans: I nearly fell.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'later'.

examples.text: Подожди, чуть позже всё сделаем.
examples.trans: Wait, we will do everything a little later.

examples.text: Позже они не успеют привезти!
examples.trans: Later they will not make it in time to deliver!

examples.text: Чуть позже схожу в ломбард.
examples.trans: A little later I will go to the pawnshop.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'ходить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'ходить'.

examples.text: Чуть позже схожу в ломбард.
examples.trans: A little later I will go to the pawnshop.

examples.text: Да, сходите.
examples.trans: Yes, go on.

examples.text: Я схожу в магазин.
examples.trans: I'll pop to the shop.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'pawnshop', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Чуть позже схожу в ломбард.
examples.trans: A little later I will go to the pawnshop.

examples.text: В восемь часов Тимур рыбу привезёт.
examples.trans: At eight o'clock Timur will bring the fish.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (root 'дать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to sell', forming an aspectual pair with 'продавать'.

examples.text: Вон в соседний ресторан продай.
examples.trans: Go sell it to the restaurant next door.

examples.text: Федя, по старой дружбе продай рыбу!
examples.trans: Fedya, for old friendship's sake, sell me the fish!

examples.text: Слушай, продай мне, сто тысяч дам!
examples.trans: Listen, sell it to me, I will give you a hundred thousand!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'stone', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Тимур, ты в драгоценных камнях разбираешься?
examples.trans: Timur, do you know about precious stones?

examples.text: Шеф, мы нашли один камень утром.
examples.trans: Chef, we found one stone this morning.

examples.text: Продам камни, а деньги поделим поровну.
examples.trans: I will sell the stones, and we will split the money equally.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (root 'елить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to divide', forming an aspectual pair with 'делить'.

examples.text: Продам камни, а деньги поделим поровну.
examples.trans: I will sell the stones, and we will split the money equally.

examples.text: И деньги поделим?
examples.trans: And split the money?

examples.text: Мы поделили яблоки пополам.
examples.trans: We split the apples in half.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'equally'.

examples.text: Поделись поровну.
examples.trans: Share it equally.

examples.text: Мы делим всё поровну.
examples.trans: We split everything equally.

examples.text: Со всеми поделись поровну, понял?
examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'казать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to say', forming an aspectual pair with 'говорить'.

examples.text: А что я своей Вике скажу?
examples.trans: And what am I going to tell my Vika?

examples.text: Я сказал, что Костя подвернул ногу.
examples.trans: I told her that Kostya twisted his ankle.

examples.text: Скажите, все с этим согласны?
examples.trans: Tell me, does everyone agree with this?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'agreeing', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Скажите, все с этим согласны?
examples.trans: Tell me, does everyone agree with this?

examples.text: Я согласен.
examples.trans: I agree.

examples.text: Я полностью согласен с вашим предложением по новому меню!
examples.trans: I completely agree with your proposal for the new menu!
